newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle fueled for Thursday launch.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle fueled for Thursday launch.

text.p: The space shuttle Discovery was fuelled early on Thursday for launch on a mission packed with scientific objectives, NASA officials said.
Launch controllers began loading the shuttle's giant strap-on fuel tank with super-cold liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen rocket fuel at about 3 a.m. EDT (0700 GMT) on Thursday.
The $2 billion reusable space freighter was scheduled to lift off its launch pad at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre at 10:41 a.m. EDT (1441 GMT).
Forecasters said there was a 40 percent chance that bad weather associated with a rare mid-summer cold front would delay Discovery's launch.
"Our primary concern is for the potential for some showers popping up in and around the area," U.S. Air Force meteorologist Scott Jacobs said.
Discovery's crew of six, which includes a Canadian researcher, were to start boarding the shuttle at about 8 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT).

During their 11-day mission, the astronauts were to study the Earth's protective ozone layer, point a telescope at Comet Hale-Bopp and test a Japanese robot arm intended for use on the international space station.
Other tasks include monitoring vegetation on Earth, growing colon cancer cells for medical research and testing positioning systems for constructing the space station.
"It's a very interesting flight," shuttle programme manager Tommy Holloway said. "We have something for everyone."
